title: Westchester Nocturne (soul-jazz, large band)
comment:
# Westchester Nocturne

70s CTI-style soul-jazz and fusion for a large band in F Dorian with an A-major bridge, 92 BPM in 4/4, 48 bars (about 2:05) that loop back to bar 1. Harmony and groove stay recognizable, and the variation comes from orchestration as the theme passes around the band.

## Form

| Section | Bars | Chords | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Night trio (vibes) | 1–8 | A loop | Vibes theme, Rhodes, bass, side stick; kick from bar 5 |
| Flute + strings | 9–16 | A loop | Flute takes the theme, vibes dyads, string pad |
| Big band (mutated loop) | 17–23 | Mutated loop | Trumpet and tenor in octaves, horn stabs, string ostinato |
| Stop | 24 | Dbmaj9♯11 | One tutti hit, then silence |
| Bridge in A (harpsichord) | 25–28 | Amaj9–F♯m11–Dmaj9♯11–C♯m7 F♯7(13) | Violins lead, harpsichord ostinato, no drums, straight feel |
| Bridge half-time | 29–32 | Bm9–E13sus–Dbmaj9♯11–C7♯9 | Half-time kit, flute counter, harp, build into 33 |
| Shout chorus | 33–39 | A loop, then mutated | Drop-2 brass soli led by trumpet, full band |
| Stop-time + bass break | 40 | C7♯9 | Tutti hits, then solo bass |
| Afterglow (harpsichord recolor) | 41–44 | Mutated loop | Vibes with French horn below, harpsichord on the loop |
| Thin back to the top | 45–48 | A loop | Back to the opening trio, kick out in 48 |

A loop: Fm9–Bb13–Ebmaj9–Dbmaj9♯11 C7♯9. Mutated loop: Fm9–Bbm9–Ebmaj9–Dbmaj9♯11 Gb13.

| Track | Part |
| --- | --- |

| Flute | Lead, countermelody, octave doubling |
